title: Production BrowserBroker grants and delegated bearer forwarding (unblocks every browser path)
summary: Give the Model Plane BrowserBroker a durable (Postgres) grant store and a production issue/acquire/revoke path. The gateway obtains a user-session grant when it creates a browser session, sends grant_id on POST /v1/agent/runs, forwards x-browser-authorization and x-inference-authorization, and derives child grants for AI runs instead of the interim session:{id} string. Add one end-to-end contract test (gateway -> model-gateway -> execution-core -> quarry-edge) in prod mode that fails on 401/403.
whyItMatters: Prod-mode Quarry requires a broker grant on every agent run and refuses to boot without a validator (SRC), yet nothing outside tests issues grants and the broker store is in memory (SRC). Until this lands, the in-app browser, the AI step/loop, co-browsing, the credential bridge, budgets carried in the grant and per-origin consent cannot work in production (INF, high confidence, not runtime-tested). This is the single highest-leverage item in the audit.

title: Gate Evaluate and raw script actions behind a grant capability and one-shot approval
summary: Make AgentAction::Evaluate (and raw CSS selector paths) read-only by default: run in an isolated world with a non-mutating document proxy, JSON-only arguments and credential-field masking. Mutating script requires an explicit grant capability plus a one-shot approval, and the planner does not see Evaluate unless the grant allows it.
whyItMatters: Quarry otherwise fails closed, but Evaluate has no approval branch, so any risky action (submit, delete, read a sensitive field) can be expressed as script and bypass the risk-classified approval model. The executor must be sound regardless of which caller reaches /step.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (CA018, CI114: three gates plus a domain allowlist for raw CDP; read-only isolated-world evaluate wrapper that cannot mutate the DOM)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Evaluate runs in Page.createIsolatedWorld against a frozen read-only proxy of document (no setters, no event dispatch), JSON-serializable args only, credential inputs masked. Raw CDP only when the grant has rawCdp=true and the method is on an allowlist; request/cookie params that carry URLs are authorised.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The Verevon UI facade refuses raw script, but Quarry accepts Evaluate{script} on normal runs: sensitive_approval_for_action handles dialog, upload and download only, and Evaluate appears in agent_routes.rs just as a label mapping (SRC, this audit). The execution-core LLM planner schema does not emit evaluate today (llm_planner.rs:53-65), so current exposure is via direct /step callers, compiled procedures and any future code-mode.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser, quarry-runtime, quarry-edge): isolated-world read-only evaluate by default; add 'evaluate_mutating' as a sensitive action needing a grant capability and one-shot approval (the same mechanism as upload/download). Model Plane: hide the action from the planner unless the grant allows it. Audit existing callers of Evaluate first.
risks: Some extraction flows may rely on mutating evaluate; audit callers before tightening.

The Model Plane half is already done: execution-core's browser.act schema (agent.rs:3479-3512) and the planner ACTION_SCHEMA (llm_planner.rs:53-65) never offer evaluate and the gateway sanitize_action denies it (browser.rs:3751), so exposure is direct service callers of /step plus Quarry's own unwired ModelPlanePlanner prompt, which advertises evaluate and pdf (mp_client.rs:383). The /step path also discards the script's return value (observation.rs:542-543), so a read-only isolated-world evaluate has no consumer there; ActionRuntime::Evaluate (action_runtime.rs:380-392) has no production caller.

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects: the gate must live in quarry-edge/quarry-runtime, not only in the planner schema, and denials must be typed Quarry errors. Grant authority belongs to the Model Plane BrowserBroker (Go), so a new sensitive action class needs a broker allowlist and proto alignment change as well as the Quarry change; approvals are strict single-action one-shot grants and sensitive actions require a parent run grant (agent_routes.rs fails with Forbidden without one). verevon.verdictReason: The Quarry-side gap is real and cheap to close, but half the approach is already shipped on the Model Plane and the read-only-evaluate design is mis-scoped to a path that discards results.

reference.corrections: Codex does not put playwright.evaluate behind a capability or an approval. It makes evaluate structurally safe instead: an isolated world, read-only wrappers, masked credential fields, a block on import(), and capped results. The consent and approval gates apply only to raw CDP: the full_cdp_access_enabled preference (default false), the enterprise requirement, and a per-origin consent that a preference can auto-answer. title: Close the gateway search-cache ZDR and tenant hole, then publish a per-feature ZDR capability matrix
summary: Phase 1 (S): the gateway /search cache key (search.rs:218-226) holds query, limit, include_answer and filters but no org or user scope, and store() runs without any ZDR check (SRC, re-read in this T2 pass); results are kept 4 h and served stale when Quarry fails. Add the authorized org id to the key, skip lookup and store for ZDR requests and ZDR orgs, and route every cache through one shared should_cache() admission rule (never cache ZDR, credentialed, action or profile requests). Phase 2 (M): declare a per-feature ZDR capability matrix with explicit refusal codes, and keep a content-free ZDR run tombstone with a default retention janitor.
whyItMatters: Two architecture rules are broken at once: ZDR must propagate, and no tenant may see another tenant's data. If smart-router results include org-scoped corpus or Data Plane vector hits (INF from the router design, not traced end to end), this is a cross-tenant disclosure, not only a ZDR gap. Phase 1 is a one-file fix.

title: ZDR-safe telemetry: span sampler, late-ZDR registry, log filter and safe/sensitive log fields in Quarry and the gateway
summary: In quarry-edge telemetry.rs add an OpenTelemetry sampler and span processor that drop spans for zdr=true requests (plus a bounded registry for runs that turn ZDR after a span started) and a tracing Layer that keeps events emitted inside ZDR spans out of the JSON fmt layer. Add one small shared helper (Rust crate plus the quarryotel Go package) whose log API forces two maps, safe (ids, enum outcomes, durations, counts) and sensitive (url, query, error text, selectors), with export sinks stripping sensitive by default. Propagate ZDR posture on internal hops as a header and NATS header, and add an operator kill switch that disables all exporters.
whyItMatters: Architecture rule: Zero-Data-Retention must propagate. It currently stops at the observability boundary: telemetry.rs always installs a JSON fmt layer and an OTLP layer with no ZDR awareness, and change_routes.rs logs the source URL inside the very branch that says ZDR is active. A leak in logs or OTLP is invisible to users and would breach ZDR contracts, and it blocks safe SIEM export and support diagnostics.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rust: a custom opentelemetry Sampler returning Drop when parent context or attributes carry zdr=true; a bounded LRU of trace ids flagged ZDR after start, checked in a SpanProcessor on_end so descendants and in-flight spans are dropped; a tracing Layer that suppresses events inside zdr=true spans; a log helper with signature log(safe: Map, sensitive: Map) where sinks drop or hash sensitive and ZDR requests always drop it. Posture travels as an internal header (for example x-verevon-zdr) and a NATS header so receivers skip request-correlated logs. A QUARRY_DISABLE_AMBIENT_TELEMETRY switch turns off every exporter.

title: Reap abandoned agent runs (idle and absolute TTL), cap concurrent runs, and make the fleet console real
summary: Add a background sweeper in quarry-edge that closes agent runs past their lease ttl_s (derived from max_runtime_s) or an idle timeout, releases the browser lease, emits a run.expired event and denies further use of the run's grant. Add per-org and global caps on concurrent runs and a tab-count warning, move the in-process run registry to durable state for multi-instance operation (non-ZDR only), and proxy /v1/fleets through the gateway so the fleet console shows real runs.
whyItMatters: Abandoned user or AI sessions currently hold a Chromium context and a live browser grant indefinitely. That is a resource leak on a shared browser host and a security exposure (a usable grant with no user present), and it grows with every agent run.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; differentiator (only Aside has code evidence, and for a local single-user product)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A global semaphore (200 concurrent runs) gates run start; a per-run counter limits active sub-agents (8); the agent is warned at 5 open tabs; each tab carries a last-activity timestamp and a sweeper closes agent tabs and sessions past an idle TTL (15 minutes) and emits an event; ephemeral sessions are retained for a fixed 15-minute window.

Only max_steps is enforced on the step path. Runs live in an in-process HashMap (new_runs) so they cannot be shared across edge instances. The lease pool holds 2 sessions on one shared Chromium. The fleet console is a stub with placeholder live views fetching /v1/fleets that the gateway does not proxy. Step budgets and fleet budget aggregation do exist.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane (quarry-edge) with a small Frontend change. Add a tokio interval task that scans the run registry and closes runs past ttl_s or an idle threshold, where last_activity is refreshed on every step, on an attached frame/WS viewer, and on user takeover; on expiry release the lease, close the CDP BrowserContext, emit run.expired and mark the grant used-up (ask Model Plane BrowserBroker to revoke). Add org-scoped and global run caps at run start returning a typed 429/RESOURCE_BUSY with retry-after. Persist run records through the existing AgentRunCheckpoint path to Postgres for non-ZDR runs so the registry works across edge instances; ZDR runs stay in memory and simply expire. Frontend: proxy /v1/fleets in the gateway and replace placeholder tiles. Implementing the ttl check also enforces max_runtime_s for agent runs.

title: Stop viewport-triggered browser relaunches: per-page emulation, a small Chromium process pool and page hygiene
summary: Apply the viewport per page or context with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride instead of closing and relaunching the single shared Chromium whenever a lease's viewport differs (None vs Some counts as different). Then replace the one process with a pool of K Chromium processes with maxOpenPages, retire-after-N-pages and a page semaphore, add a /health probe that really opens a page, and size the lease pool from config instead of the hard-coded 2. In the same page-attach path add Page.setWebLifecycleState(active) and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true) and a fixed per-lease viewport so coordinates and screenshots are deterministic.
whyItMatters: ensure_browser closes the browser and clears every session's pages, egress receipts, dialogs and telemetry when the viewport changes, so two concurrent in-app browser or agent sessions with different viewport options can destroy each other's live sessions. The in-app browser and AI runs need predictable capacity and crash containment; pages that check focus or visibility (menus, chat widgets, video) also behave unpredictably without focus emulation.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Pool of N browser processes; each tracks open pages and pages served. New contexts go to the least-loaded process below maxOpenPages; after retireAfter pages a process stops taking work and closes when idle; pre/post launch and page hooks run in a fixed order; /health opens about:blank in a fresh context with a deadline. Per page on attach: Page.enable, DOM.enable, Network.enable, Page.setWebLifecycleState('active'), Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true), Target.setAutoAttach(flatten). Rust shape: Vec<BrowserSlot{proc, open, served, retiring}> behind a Mutex plus a tokio Semaphore for pages.

title: Enforce cost and runtime budgets in the Quarry executor, meter browser time, and clamp crawls to the remaining entitlement
summary: The run contract carries max_cost_usd and max_runtime_s, but only max_steps is enforced on the /step path, defaults are unbounded and browser minutes are not metered (SRC). Quarry, as the executor, reserves on run start, charges per step and per browser-second, stops gracefully at the cap with a typed BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and clamps crawl/batch page limits and requests per minute to the remaining entitlement. Model Plane cost-core passes the remaining budget inside the grant and reconciles; org default caps arrive via the policy claims of F-t2-022.
whyItMatters: Agents with live browsers and paid providers can run up unbounded cost. docs/WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:50-53 says max_cost_usd is enforced, but the HTTP step path does not enforce it (doc/code divergence, SRC). Apify (charge within cap, DOC) and Firecrawl (reserve then settle, SRC) both enforce in the executor.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: On session create: check entitlement, reserve a concurrency slot and estimated cost. On stop: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE the session row, compute duration-based cost (separate rates for human, AI-driven and ZDR use) and mark it settled; a periodic sweep settles sessions whose stop was missed. Per step: add action and LLM cost to a run-scoped accumulator and fail the step with BUDGET_EXCEEDED when it passes max_cost_usd. || Merged items add: Caller sets a max total charge per run. Before each billable step the executor calls charge(event, count), which returns how many units are still chargeable within the cap; when the cap is reached it finishes the current step, persists partial results and ends with a budget-exhausted status. For time-billed browser sessions Firecrawl reserves the full TTL at the per-minute rate before the first prompt (402 if the balance is short), re-rates sessions that used prompts, settles actual duration on stop and releases the remainder. || At submit: limit = min(requested, remaining_entitlement) and both values are stored on the job. maxDiscoveryDepth bounds link depth; per-crawl maxConcurrency and delay feed the scheduler; usage counters are sharded so huge crawls do not contend on one row; results and state carry expires_at (default 24 h).
